paper.title_en: Cross-Moment Consistency and the Fifth Adler Coefficient in Hadronic Tau Decays
paper.abstract_en: The unknown coefficient $c_{5,1}$ controls the first omitted fifth-order term in fixed-order analyses of inclusive hadronic $τ$ decays. We determine what the four known Adler coefficients can actually test. For any normalized polynomial weight, the fixed-order Adler-to-moment map is triangular with unit diagonal. Hence one common Adler-coefficient error reaches every moment with the same absolute size, and a multi-weight relative test reduces to one absolute tolerance. For three representative weights, a ten-percent test resolves $c_{5,1}$ only to about $\pm24$; the closest contour-improved test is weaker by more than an order of magnitude. Moreover, any continuation that preserves the observed sign of the direct Padé/Shanks defects gives $c_{5,1}\geq378.03$, so values near $280$ require additional structure. A calibration-and-falsification protocol applied to a simplified Beneke--Jamin-type pure-power ansatz gives the conditional estimate $c_{5,1}=248\pm30\,(\mathrm{struct})\pm74\,(\mathrm{method})=248\pm80$. At the physical order its central value coincides algebraically with the exact four-parameter fit; the protocol adds a falsifiable admissibility test and a method uncertainty, not new coefficient information.
